deviations_from_adr: ADR contracts §3 suggested web/src/screens/kanban-board.js could optionally import ../../../src/core/view-config.ts's enumValuesForSelectField directly (precedent: records-form.js/apps-schema.js/Floor2Viewer.jsx already do this). Instead, kanban-board.js carries its OWN small pure mirror (readSelectEnum) of the same enum-reading logic, following the list-view-panel.js precedent (byte-mirror + a documented rationale) rather than the direct-import precedent. Rationale: keeps kanban-board.js consistent with its sibling list-view-panel.js (which mirrors operatorsForFieldType/isServerSortable the same way) rather than mixing both patterns in the same feature; the mirrored logic is a 4-line pure read with no drift risk (a single properties[key].enum lookup, unlike the larger operator tables). Verified harmless via a manual Docker-isolation build (rsync web/ + cp src/core/ + vite build) — clean either way. No functional difference from the ADR's intent.

friction_events: Fresh worktree had no node_modules at root or web/ — required `npm install` (root) and `npm install` (web/) before any tsc/vitest/build command would run. Consistent with the durable memory note 'npm install после merge'.

First cut of ci/checks/kanban-write-via-record-put.sh used `return "${errors}"` from a bash function combined with `check_file || true; TOTAL_ERRORS=$((TOTAL_ERRORS + $?))` — the `|| true` swallows the real exit code, so `$?` was always 0/1 from the `true`, not the function's actual error count. Fixed by having the check functions `echo` their integer count (captured via command substitution) instead of relying on a bash function 'return' as an error counter.

ci/checks/kanban-write-via-record-put.sh also had SCRIPT_DIR/ROOT resolved as `${SCRIPT_DIR}/..` (one level) instead of `${SCRIPT_DIR}/../..` (the script lives in ci/checks/, needs two levels up to reach the repo root) — caught immediately by a wrong-path SKIP in the real (non-self-test) run and fixed.

ci/checks/ux/kanban-ux-gate.sh's no-jargon detector initially false-positived on kanban-board.jsx's own top-of-file prose comment (a multi-line /* ... */ block with no per-line '*'/'//' prefix, unlike JSDoc-style comments elsewhere) because the line-prefix comment-stripping approach (grep -vE '^\s*(//|\*)') does not recognize an UNPREFIXED continuation line inside a block comment as a comment line. Fixed by replacing the line-prefix heuristic with a small awk state machine that tracks in-comment state across /* ... */ spans and blanks any code content found there, regardless of per-line prefix.
